keyMessage.found: HIS and Active Directory will not recover within tolerable downtime and no restore has been tested.
keyMessage.closes: Agree recovery objectives for HIS, PACS, and LIS and test a restore with integrity checks.

gapFindings.title: No recovery plan based on agreed recovery objectives
gapFindings.statement: Recovery objectives and restore order are not agreed, so no plan matches what HIS, PACS, and Active Directory need.

supportingFacts.fact: HIS and Active Directory will not recover within tolerable downtime.
A recovery site or cloud option was not confirmed.
No restore order or end-of-recovery criteria are defined.

extent.notChecked: Recovery of LIS and ERP was not profiled

gapFindings.consequence: Recovery after ransomware is unplanned, so clinical systems return late and in the wrong order.

likelihood.rationale: No plan exists for Criticality A systems and the threat is active.

ops.rationale: Unplanned recovery stops or slows hospital operations.

fin.rationale: Unplanned recovery adds recovery cost and revenue loss.

legal.rationale: Unplanned recovery triggers reporting duties or regulator questions.

rep.rationale: Unplanned recovery damages patient and public trust.

safety.rationale: Unplanned recovery delays or disrupts patient care.

data.rationale: Unplanned recovery exposes sensitive health records.

notApplicable.prevent: Recurrence is addressed by the related Governance and Process actions.
notApplicable.exceptions: No system is known to be unable to meet the control.

gapFindings.title: Backups and restored systems are never verified
gapFindings.statement: No restore has been tested, so CMC does not know whether backups work or how long recovery takes.

supportingFacts.fact: No restore test ran on HIS, Microsoft 365, or Active Directory in 12 months.
Restore tests do not measure actual recovery time.
Backup jobs are monitored only in part.

gapFindings.consequence: Restores fail or bring back infected data, and clinical staff work without a tested manual fallback.

likelihood.rationale: Restore testing is Poor on Criticality A systems and the threat is active.

ops.rationale: Failed restore stops or slows hospital operations.

fin.rationale: Failed restore adds recovery cost and revenue loss.

legal.rationale: Failed restore triggers reporting duties or regulator questions.

rep.rationale: Failed restore damages patient and public trust.

safety.rationale: Failed restore delays or disrupts patient care.

data.rationale: Limited direct effect in this scenario.

notApplicable.find: The affected systems or units are already identified.
notApplicable.exceptions: No system is known to be unable to meet the control.

keyMessage.found: No process tells patients, partners, and regulators how recovery is progressing.
keyMessage.closes: Define the recovery communication process and approve a spokesperson.

gapFindings.title: No process to communicate during recovery
gapFindings.statement: No process or spokesperson informs patients, referring hospitals, and regulators as services return.

supportingFacts.fact: No recovery communication process or approved spokesperson exists.

extent.notChecked: Existing stakeholder lists were not reviewed

gapFindings.consequence: Recovery updates are informal and inconsistent, which prolongs loss of trust.

improvementActions.action: Agree recovery objectives for HIS, PACS, and LIS and write a recovery plan with restore order
Evaluate a recovery site or cloud recovery option for HIS and Active Directory
Check backup integrity before every restore and verify restored systems before release
Document paper-based downtime procedures for the wards
Define the recovery communication process and approve a spokesperson
